title: Nabla ambient AI scribe reduced physicians' note-writing time in a three-arm randomized trial at UCLA Health
summary: In a UCLA Health randomized trial of 238 outpatient physicians, the Nabla ambient scribe cut time-in-note by 9.5% against usual care; DAX Copilot showed no significant change.
account: UCLA Health ran a pragmatic randomized trial of two ambient AI scribes from 4 November 2024 to 3 January 2025. The trial team assigned 238 outpatient physicians in 14 specialties to Microsoft Dragon Ambient eXperience (DAX) Copilot, to Nabla, or to usual care. The scribes recorded visits and drafted notes inside the Epic record. Nabla was used in 29.5% of 23,653 visits. Physicians who used Nabla cut their time-in-note by 9.5% against the control group (95% confidence interval 1.8% to 17.2%). The DAX group showed no significant change in time-in-note. Survey scores for burnout and task load suggested improvement with both scribes, but the authors write that these secondary results need confirmation in larger trials. Physicians reported clinically significant inaccuracies "occasionally", and one mild adverse event was reported. The UCLA Department of Medicine and other UCLA units funded the trial, which ran at a single academic health system over two months.
purpose: Nabla is built to record clinical encounters and draft visit notes so that clinicians spend less time on documentation. The measured time saving is that purpose.
location: UCLA Health outpatient clinics, Los Angeles, California, United States

ratings.reason: Physicians who used Nabla spent 9.5% less time writing notes than physicians in usual care.
The health system recovered documentation time across 23,653 visits in the Nabla arm without other changes to clinic work.

ai_role.statement: Physicians were randomized to a scribe or to usual care, and the trial compared changes in time-in-note against the control group. The trial isolates the effect of offering the scribe. Physicians chose when to use it, and they used Nabla in 29.5% of visits.
